findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion covering the docs updates (docs/plan-review-gate.md close-gate section and docs/llm-framework.md) so every listed deliverable has a covering criterion.

findings.finding: The docs deliverables (docs/plan-review-gate.md close-gate section, docs/llm-framework.md) are listed in Scope but no acceptance criterion covers them, leaving a described deliverable without a proving criterion.
scenarios: Executor lands code + tests, closes the epic, docs never updated because no criterion demanded it
findings.suggested_fix: Add: '- [ ] docs/plan-review-gate.md documents the three-stage close gate (DET floor, candidate filter, haiku screen + disposition rule) and docs/llm-framework.md references the new epic_bug_screen prompt/schema.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an [operator-attested] acceptance criterion capturing the manual live-haiku calibration run (with a concrete attestation — run id/timestamp/verdict tally recorded on this ticket) so the new live model path is proven, not only its faked substitute.
evidence: 'All regression/unit tests drive the screen through a FAKE forced-choice verdict map (deterministic, no live model)'
'the live haiku path is exercised only in manual calibration runs recorded on this ticket'
No AC captures the manual calibration attestation
findings.finding: The live haiku screen path is a new LLM code path that all regression/unit tests bypass via a FAKE forced-choice verdict map; the only production-path exercise is 'manual calibration runs recorded on this ticket', but no acceptance criterion requires or attests that live run — so the ACs can all go green without the live model path ever executing.
findings.location: Testing: 'drive the screen through a FAKE forced-choice verdict map ... the live haiku path is exercised only in manual calibration runs recorded on this ticket'; Acceptance Criteria
scenarios: Screen prompt/model-class wiring has a defect that the fake-verdict tests can never catch; epic closes as done with the live path unproven
findings.suggested_fix: Add: '- [ ] [operator-attested] A live haiku calibration run over the regression fixtures is recorded on this ticket (run timestamp + per-bug verdict tally), confirming the screen exercises the model-class-configured live path end-to-end.'

findings.checklist_item: Add a live/end-to-end acceptance criterion (or a NAMED follow-up ticket) that exercises the real haiku screen call through the normalizing validator at least once, or document why the fake forced-choice verdict map is faithful to the production model's output contract.
evidence: Plan: 'All regression/unit tests drive the screen through a FAKE forced-choice verdict map (deterministic, no live model) ... the live haiku path is exercised only in manual calibration runs recorded on this ticket.'

Mitigating design: the screen 'degrades open (log + skip), never blocks the close by itself; the DET floor is the hard tier' — so a broken live path degrades open rather than closing-green a broken blocking path, which lowers but does not eliminate the coverage gap.
No acceptance criterion asserts the live haiku call end-to-end (real model -> normalizing validator -> A/B/C verdict).
findings.finding: The haiku relevance screen is a new logic path with a live model boundary, but every automated regression/unit test drives it through a FAKE forced-choice verdict map; the live haiku path (does the real model reliably emit the A/B/C + citation contract the normalizing validator expects) is exercised 'only in manual calibration runs recorded on this ticket,' with no live/end-to-end acceptance criterion. The proxy-validation carve-outs are only partially met: the live exercise is not deferred to a NAMED child ticket, and the stated rationale ('matching the repo's LLM-test idiom') justifies the offline unit idiom but does not argue the fake verdict map is faithful to production model behavior.
findings.location: Testing section ('All regression/unit tests drive the screen through a FAKE forced-choice verdict map ... the live haiku path is exercised only in manual calibration runs') + Acceptance Criteria
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC: 'A live haiku screen call is exercised at least once end-to-end (real model -> epic_bug_screen_verdict normalizing validator -> A/B/C + citation) and recorded on this ticket', or record the calibration run as a checked acceptance artifact rather than an informal manual note.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the concrete read primitive that yields the epic's FIRST in_progress transition timestamp (a raw ticket-event read, or a new reducer-folded state field), since compiled show_ticket state and the _reads facade expose no such timestamp today; state it in Approach stage 2 / Scope so the 'created-after-first-in_progress' AC is grounded.
evidence: Compiled ticket-state schema (src/rebar/reducer/_state.py:6-60 make_initial_state) exposes created_at, status, and claimed_session (the latter folded on the open->in_progress edge per _processors.py:187-208) but NO timestamp for the first in_progress transition.

The _reads facade (src/rebar/_reads.py) exposes show_ticket / list_tickets / deps / search / ready / next_batch — none returns per-transition timestamps; the DET floor already uses _reads.list_tickets(parent=...) but there is no analogous read for transition timing.

search_files for 'first_in_progress', 'status_history', 'STATUS_TRANSITION', and a ticket-store 'list_events' across src/rebar returned no ticket-event read primitive (the only list_events is the Gerrit client, review_bot/gerrit_client.py:315).
By contrast the same filter's link half (any-relation/any-depth/both-direction) IS groundable via _reads.deps + graph/_graph.py, so this gap is specific to the timing half.
findings.finding: The candidate-filter criterion 'created after the epic's FIRST in_progress transition' commits to a first-in_progress-transition timestamp, but the plan names no read primitive that surfaces it and the compiled ticket state does not carry one.
findings.location: Approach stage 2 (DET candidate filter) + Acceptance Criteria line 2 ('created-after-first-in_progress') + Testing ('timing window uses FIRST in_progress transition')
scenarios: Implementer builds the filter from show_ticket's compiled state and finds no transition timestamp, then either silently substitutes created_at/claimed-at (changing the semantics the AC pins) or must add an unplanned raw-event read.
A bug created BEFORE the epic went in_progress but linked into the subtree is the intended catch; if the timing input is wrong, the OR-branch masking hides the miscomputation and it ships uncaught.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the candidate-filter timing behavior when the epic has NO first-in_progress transition event (distinct from a compacted-but-recoverable one): state whether the timing arm falls open or closed, and confirm the STATUS-event read includes retired tombstones so a merely-compacted transition is still anchored.
evidence: Plan: 'created after the epic's FIRST in_progress transition OR linked any-relation/any-depth'
event_metrics.py:11 documents 'Compaction may retire a folded event to a *.json.retired tombstone'; the transition is recoverable via include_retired but only if the event ever existed

ABSENCE: the plan states no behavior for an epic with no first-in_progress event — whether the OR's timing arm then evaluates to include-all (fan-out blowup past the cited p90/max) or include-none (relying solely on the link arm, which by the plan's own stage-1 reasoning misses unlinked orphans)
findings.finding: The candidate filter's timing clause ('created after the epic's FIRST in_progress transition') does not specify the fallback when the epic has NO in_progress transition event at all (an epic closed directly from open, or one predating the workflow), where the timing anchor is absent rather than merely compacted.
findings.location: Approach stage 2 (DET candidate filter) / AC line 'Candidate filter implements exactly: ... (created-after-first-in_progress OR linked-any-relation-any-depth)'
scenarios: An epic transitioned open→closed without ever entering in_progress
An epic created before the in_progress-tracking workflow existed, so no such STATUS event was ever written
findings.suggested_fix: Add to stage 2: read the first open→in_progress STATUS event WITH retired tombstones (include_retired=True, per event_metrics._event_files); when the epic has no such event at all, fall back to the epic's creation timestamp (or the link-arm alone) as the timing anchor and note the choice explicitly.

findings.finding: The verifier's disposition test ('a filed+linked+reasoned deferral — accepted-with-reason, superseded-by, proven-pre-existing — SATISFIES') does not specify the PROVENANCE/representation of these disposition signals: are they structured link-relation types / status values the verifier reads deterministically, or prose the LLM must infer from the bug body? The must-pass fixtures (e6a0 superseded-by 4702; 30d3 proven-pre-existing) hinge on this being recognizable.
findings.location: Approach stage 3, 'Verifier directive: block only a defect-in-deliverable with NO recorded disposition'
findings.suggested_fix: Enumerate the concrete disposition signals as either link-relation types (e.g. superseded_by edge) or an explicit status/reason field, and state that the verifier retrieves them via show_ticket; note which form each must-pass fixture uses.

findings.finding: Forwarding A-verdict evidence to the completion verifier requires weaving it into the verifier's assembled context, which is built in gate_ops.py:completion_precheck (the `context` field of completion_precheck_output) — a consumer outside completion.py that the plan does not enumerate. The verifier is a workflow prompt step whose only ticket context is the fenced `context` string assembled by completion_precheck (via operations.assemble_context); the completion_precheck_output schema requires `context` and forbids additionalProperties.
findings.location: Approach step 3 / Scope: 'Forward A-verdicts to the completion verifier as compact evidence ... src/rebar/llm/completion.py (... evidence forwarding)'
findings.suggested_fix: Specify how the compact candidates reach the verifier: append them into the fenced `context` assembled in completion_precheck (no schema change), or add an evidence field to completion_precheck_output (schema edit) — and name that file in Scope.

findings.finding: The plan's new 'Verifier directive' and compact-candidate adjudication protocol are decision rules the LLM completion-verifier executes from its system prompt, but the plan's Scope does not include editing that prompt (reviewers/completion_verifier.md) and does not state where the directive is injected — an instruction-locality gap between the decision rule and the prompt/schema that needs it.
findings.location: Scope section (lists completion.py, epic_bug_screen.py, completion_sidecar.py, docs; omits the verifier prompt); Approach stage 3 'Verifier directive: ...'.

findings.finding: The verifier's disposition SATISFIES vocabulary ('accepted-with-reason, superseded-by, proven-pre-existing') is an enum-like value set the LLM verifier must key on, but its value vocabulary and representation are never defined and correspond to no real enum: the link relations are supersedes/discovered_from/caused_by/etc (no 'superseded-by', no 'accepted-with-reason', no 'proven-pre-existing'), and the close_class enum (regression/plan_defect/.../preexisting/...) exists only on a CLOSED bug while the rule targets OPEN/IN_PROGRESS deferrals.
findings.location: Approach stage 3: 'Verifier directive: block only a defect-in-deliverable with NO recorded disposition; a filed+linked+reasoned deferral (accepted-with-reason, superseded-by, proven-pre-existing) SATISFIES'; AC line 'blocks only undispositioned deliverable-defects'.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the invented tokens with a concrete, store-grounded rule: a disposition is SATISFIED when the bug carries (a) a supersedes/duplicates link to the epic or its replacement, OR (b) a reasoned comment/description asserting pre-existence, judged for substance by the verifier — and is NEVER satisfied by close_class alone. State that the verifier retrieves these via show_ticket, and map each regression fixture to the exact signal it uses.

findings.finding: The haiku screen emits a structured forced-choice ({A/B/C} + one-line citation) but the plan does not specify its structured-output contract: no reviewer prompt file (with `outputs:`), no registered output_schema in contracts.py, and no normalizing validator for the forced choice — all three being the established idiom for every other forced-choice LLM sub-call (overlap_verdict).
findings.location: Approach stage 3 (haiku relevance screen); Scope 'new module ... e.g. src/rebar/llm/epic_bug_screen.py'; AC 'forced-choice output with citation'.
